title: Consumption Contracts and Fidelity Mapping Guide
author: Marina Liu
content:
Summary

This guide describes the consumption contract primitives and the canonical mapping from fidelity tiers to contract parameters used across Redwood products (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private). It is intended for product managers, solutions engineers, billing, and SREs who implement and operate SLO-aligned consumption controls: per-route SLOs, token budgets, fidelity budgets, and fallback policies.

Goals

1. Provide a standard set of fidelity tiers that map predictably to model variants, latency targets, and cost multipliers.
2. Define contract primitives that are pluggable across the Redwood Console, Redwood API, and Smart Router.
3. Give step-by-step rollout and monitoring guidance for migrating customers to fidelity-aware contracts without regressions.

Scope

- Applies to all new and renewal Hosted API and Dedicated contracts after 2027-07-01.
- Private deployments should adopt the same primitives; implementation details may vary by on-prem package.
- Does NOT include marketplace third-party add-on pricing (handled in pricing-and-packaging).

Key definitions

- Fidelity tier: An explicit expectation for output quality/recall for a given route (examples: exploratory, standard, high-fidelity).
- Consumption contract: Machine-readable agreement (SLOs + budget + fallback rules) that governs routing, billing, and automatic degradations.
- SLO budget: Latency/availability targets expressed as p50/p95/p99 measurements and an error budget for automatic adjustments.
- Fallback policy: Ordered list of compatible variants to route to when the primary variant violates capacity or latency constraints.

Fidelity tiers (canonical)

| Tier name | Typical model variants | p95 latency target (hosted) | Quality guard (eval delta budget) | Cost multiplier | Suggested use cases |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| exploratory | small quantized variants (e.g., mfast-7b-q) | 250 ms | None (best-effort) | 0.6x | Low-cost experimentation, dev sandbox |
| standard | mid variants (e.g., mstd-13b, community-13b) | 400 ms | -2% relative eval score allowed | 1x | Product features where moderate fidelity suffices |
| high-fidelity | large variants (e.g., mpro-70b, verified-70b) | 900 ms | <= 0.5% eval regression | 3x | Customer-facing, legal/regulatory outputs |
| safety-critical | audited variants (FIPS/HSM-backed) | 1200 ms | 0% regression tolerance | 5x | Compliance-bound, PII/PHI outputs |

Contract primitives (machine-readable fields)

Each contract is expressed as a small JSON doc (below shows canonical fields). Implementations in the Redwood Console and Redwood API read these fields and configure Smart Router rules, costing, and fallback.

Required fields: 
- route_id (string)
- fidelity_tier (string: exploratory|standard|high-fidelity|safety-critical)
- slo_p95_ms (integer)
- token_budget_per_hour (integer)
- cost_ceiling_usd_per_1m_tokens (number)
- fallback_variants (ordered list of variant IDs)
- auto_fallback_threshold_pct (number) // percent of slo breaches that trigger fallback

Optional fields:
- ttl_days (integer) // how long this contract applies before renewal check
- quality_guard_eval_tag (string) // reference to eval set in Optimize
- regional_preference (string list)

Mapping rules (canonical algorithm)

When a new contract is created for a route, the system runs the following mapping steps (pseudocode / high level):
1) Input: route traffic profile (p50/p95 token lengths, peak rps), customer tier (self-serve/enterprise), data sensitivity label.
2) Choose base fidelity: if data sensitivity == PHI or regulated -> safety-critical; elif enterprise + SLA -> high-fidelity; elif peak rps > 500 && cost constraints flagged -> standard; else exploratory.
3) Assign slo_p95_ms using fidelity tier table. For Dedicated/Private, apply +15% latency buffer to account for network egress and private infra variability.
4) Calculate token_budget_per_hour = max(ceil(peak_rps * avg_tokens), default_min) subject to customer quota.
5) cost_ceiling_usd_per_1m_tokens = base_cost_multiplier(fidelity) * catalog_model_unit_cost(route_profile).
6) Populate fallback_variants using the compatibility matrix from Model Onboarding (see related_pages).

Rollout and migration playbook (per-customer)

1) Discovery (PM/SE): Collect route traffic fingerprint and expectations. Capture existing anomalies and known prompts (10 canonical prompts).
2) Proposal: Create a draft consumption contract and present to customer with 30/60/90 day migration options. Include explicit eval tag used for quality guard.
3) Canary: Configure 5% traffic canary for 72 hours with detailed tracing. Monitor p95, error-rate, and eval-set scoring.
4) Expand to 25% for 7 days if canary green. Watch for regressions in Redwood Optimize alerts.
5) Full cutover with automatic 2-hour fallback window enabled. If auto_fallback_threshold_pct exceeded for >1 hour, Smart Router rolls back traffic.
6) Post-migration QBR: capture cost delta, latency delta, and quality regressions. Add remediation/adjustments to contract if needed.

Monitoring and alerts

Essential dashboards (Console panels):
- Per-route SLO dashboard: p50/p95/p99, token throughput, token budget consumption %
- Fidelity guard dashboard: eval score vs baseline, regression alerts (>=0.5% drop)
- Cost drift dashboard: estimated monthly spend vs contract ceiling

Suggested alert thresholds:
- p95 > slo_p95_ms for 5m -> Severity P2 (notify SRE + customer success)
- token_budget_per_hour > 80% -> Severity P3 (notify billing and SE)
- eval score drop >= 1% -> Severity P1 (notify PM, Optimize, and model-owner)

Billing and metering examples

Billing for fidelity uses a two-part mapping: unit rate per 1M tokens adjusted by fidelity multiplier + per-route premium for guaranteed SLOs. Example mapping JSON (policy stored in billing service):

```
{
  "route_id": "orders-completion-v1",
  "fidelity_tier": "high-fidelity",
  "unit_rate_per_1m_tokens_usd": "0.40", 
  "fidelity_multiplier": "3.0",
  "slo_premium_usd_per_month": "250"
}
```

CLI example: create a contract via redwoodctl (example)

redwoodctl contract create --route orders-completion-v1 --fidelity high-fidelity \n  --slo-p95-ms 900 --token-budget-hour 50000 --cost-ceiling-1m 30.0 \n  --fallback "mstd-13b,mfast-7b" --quality-guard-tag qset-orders-v2

Infrastructure considerations

- Smart Router must have the latest compatibility matrix synced hourly from Model Onboarding.
- Serving Runtime must expose per-variant queue depth and estimated per-token latency for accurate auto-fallback decisions.
- For Dedicated pools, autoscaling policies must include a reserved headroom of 10% for high-fidelity routes.

Ownership and escalation

- Product (owner): defines fidelity tiers, base multipliers, and canonical contract shape.
- Billing: owns billing mapping and unit-rate changes.
- SRE/Runtime: implements autoscale and latency telemetry hooks.
- Customer Success / SE: runs migrations and QBRs.

Escalation path: 
- Severity P1: PM -> SE Lead -> SRE Eng -> Engineering Manager (15m response SLA)
- Billing disputes: Billing Rep -> Finance Ops -> Legal (48h SLA for initial response)

Appendix B — migration timeline template

- Week 0: Discovery and contract PRD
- Week 1: Canary configuration (5%)
- Week 2: Canary analysis and adjustments
- Week 3: Expanded canary (25%)
- Week 4: Full cutover and monitoring phase
